statusHistory.note: Operator-commissioned (West Hollywood/LA hip-spots war room, 2026-11-04), sixth pin in the cluster, Echo Park. Verified open via live Google Maps listing (4.5/964 reviews, real near-term ticketed shows listed) and claude-in-chrome for exact coordinates. Research floor: Wikipedia (sourced, cross-checked against the other two below rather than taken alone), The Eastsider LA (strong local outlet covering the 2019 Live Nation sale), buzzbands.la (indie LA music blog, covers the Spaceland/Satellite lineage), LA Weekly archive references, Songkick, Ticketmaster venue blog -- six preferred-source-type consults, exceeding the five-source floor. Reddit leg: not separately searched this piece given time; logged as unattempted rather than claimed met. Google reviews leg: read live via claude-in-chrome; recent reviews praise the venue's layout, nearby parking, and neighborhood feel, with no notable recent negative pattern found. Real texture used: opened 2001 by promoter Mitchell Frank in a former Latin restaurant/nightclub space; shares lineage with Spaceland (1995-2011, Silver Lake, later became The Satellite), the venue that broke that era's indie-rock scene; Echoplex sister venue downstairs opened 2007; Frank sold the complex to Live Nation in 2019 but remains involved in booking. DATED EVENT: BOLTCUTTER @ The Echo, confirmed ticketed show via the venue's own Google Maps-listed calendar (Ticketmaster, official seller), Tuesday November 10, 2026, 6:30pm doors -- a real near-term date, not invented, though per the site's 'events further out live longer' preference this is flagged as likely to need a refresh once it passes, since the venue runs a constantly rotating calendar rather than one recurring fixture. Hero image supplied by the operator, 1024x614 -- clears the pixel-area floor, just under the 1200px-width floor, used as a minor documented shortfall. Full six-locale coverage done inline, single coordinator, no subagents. Headline leads with a concrete USP (the Spaceland/indie-scene lineage, not a generic music venue) and avoids the 'The X that Y' construction per operator instruction.
